description: Given an integer n, return all the structurally unique BSTs which have exactly n nodes of unique values from 1 to n. Return the root nodes of all possible trees.
intuition: For a range of values [1..n], each value i can be the root. Its left subtree uses values [1..i-1] and its right subtree uses [i+1..n]. Generate all left and right subtrees recursively, then combine every left-right pair with root i. This Cartesian product approach naturally produces all valid BSTs.
approach: Use recursive divide-and-conquer. For each possible root value i, recursively generate all left subtrees from [start, i-1] and all right subtrees from [i+1, end]. Combine each left-right pair with root i.

Input: n = 3

build(1, 3):

    build(2,3): rootVal=2: left=[null], right=build(3,3)

    root=2, left=null, right=TreeNode(3) -> [TreeNode(2, null, 3)]
    rootVal=3: left=build(2,2)=[TreeNode(2)], right=[null]
    -> [TreeNode(3, TreeNode(2), null)]
    right=build(2,3) = [2->3, 3->2]
  root=1, left=null, right=2->3 -> tree: 1->null,2->null,3
  root=1, left=null, right=3->2 -> tree: 1->null,3->2,null
  rootVal=2: left=build(1,1)=[TreeNode(1)], right=build(3,3)=[TreeNode(3)]
  -> tree: 2->1,3
  rootVal=3: left=build(1,2) = 2 trees, right=[null] -> 2 more trees

Total: 5 unique BSTs
explanation:
1. For range [lo, hi], try each value i as the root.
2. Recursively build all left subtrees from [lo, i-1].
3. Recursively build all right subtrees from [i+1, hi].
4. Combine each (left, right) pair with root i.
5. Base case: empty range returns [None] (null subtree).
hints: For each possible root, the left subtree uses smaller values and right uses larger.
Recursively generate all possible left and right subtrees.
Combine every pair of left and right subtrees with the chosen root.
